prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a downward-tilted egocentric view of a paved street with a person in a blue top immediately to the bottom-right (0.3–0.6 m away, within arm's reach) and a second person in jeans carrying a brown handbag walking ahead and slightly left (1.0–1.5 m from the camera wearer and roughly 1.0–1.5 m ahead of the right-side person). Both companions face away in the direction of travel with their heads cropped out of the top and right frame boundaries, while the camera wearer's own lower leg and white sandal appear at the bottom-center (0.8–1.0 m below the head-mounted camera). Across the 5 frames, the person ahead retreats farther away (fading from mid-grey to near-black by frame 4 and exiting by frame 5) while the person on the right moves closer and enters physical contact as the camera wearer's right hand grasps their left forearm in frames 4–5 (both appearing bright white at ~0.4 m). Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground silhouettes of the raised hand, torso, and dangling handbag against the flat ground plane, as well as the continuous downward distance gradient of the pavement. However, it is unreliable where the very close right-side person saturates to uniform white (losing depth separation between the camera wearer's grasping hand and the companion's sleeve in frame 4) and where the retreating person's shoes blend into the dark background pavement in frame 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies the two walking companions—one at the top-center (1.0–2.5 m ahead, facing away) and one at the bottom-right (0.3–0.6 m away, within arm's reach and facing forward/left)—along with the leading person's left-side handbag (~1.2 m away) and the camera wearer's own lower leg at the bottom-center (~0.9 m below). Over the 5 frames, the top-center mask shrinks and exits the upper boundary as that person walks farther ahead, while the bottom-right mask expands across the right half of the frame as the right-side companion steps closer and the camera wearer's right hand holds their left forearm in frames 4–5. All people have their heads and upper or lower bodies partially cropped by the frame edges, and in frames 3–5 the right-side person's torso and the camera wearer's grasping arm occlude the pavement and the companion's lower legs. While the map cleanly delineates the boundaries of the foreground actors and separates the carried bag from the walker's hip in frames 1–2, it exhibits severe classification and grouping errors that are obvious in RGB. Specifically, it mislabels the brown handbag as 'skateboard' in frame 1 and overlapping 'handbag'/'suitcase' in frame 2, merges the brown bag into the 'person' mask in frame 3, misclassifies the camera wearer's own leg as a 'bottle' in frame 4, and inconsistently splits or merges the camera wearer's grasping arm and the companion's torso in frames 4–5.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map localizes the articulated magenta hand keypoints of the companion on the bottom-right (0.3–0.6 m away, within arm's reach) across all 5 frames, alongside sparse yellow body keypoints for the retreating person ahead (~1.2–1.5 m away in frame 2) and the right-side companion's left arm (~0.4–0.5 m away in frame 4). In frame 1, the right-side person's left hand is raised open at ~0.4 m in front of and below the camera wearer, then lowers toward the bottom-right in frames 2–3 before curling into a closed fist at chest/waist level in frames 4–5 while the camera wearer's right hand grasps their left forearm. In frame 2, the yellow torso and leg keypoints on the person ahead reflect a body facing away from the camera wearer, though with noisy, bunched joints near the upper crop boundary where the head and shoulders are out of view. The map makes the fine 3D finger articulation and palm orientation of the companion's left hand immediately explicit in every frame, even when motion-blurred or angled near the bottom edge in frames 2–3. However, it is highly unreliable for full-body tracking under severe egocentric cropping and close-range occlusion, completely missing the leading person in frames 1 and 3–5, failing to detect the camera wearer's own leg or grasping right hand in frames 4–5, and hallucinating disconnected yellow keypoints on the patterned shirt in frame 2.
